title: Updated needed for newer OpenSSL / newer Asio
description:
@qulogic opened [issue 14 over at my AsioHeaders repo](https://github.com/eddelbuettel/asioheaders/issues/14) as an update appears needed for OpenSSL 4 as seen in the freshest Fedora release.

So I prepared a release candidate AsioHeader 1.38.4-0, based on the newest / current stable Asio headers releases. It passes with two of its CRAN reverse dependencies, but croaks for `websocket`.   There is an older alias `io_service` in use here which Asio already [deprecated in release 1.33](https://think-async.com/Asio/asio-1.38.2/doc/asio/history.html#asio.history.asio_1_38_2) (!!).

Could team websocket please look into an update from your side?  I would expect CRAN to come knocking eventually anyway.

My release candidate of AsioHeaders is at https://dirk.eddelbuettel.com/tmp/AsioHeaders_1.38.4-0.tar.gz for your persusal, and in the corresponding branch.   

Thanks in advance for your consideration.

PS Subject corrected. It's OpenSSL, not curl, that bites.

title: ability to view later list/queue?
description:
I was testing consumption of some data streams, and it was a learning process. While doing it, I instantiated a `WebSocket$new()` but while developing it I created objects, they failed (my mistakes). SFSG, learning is fun.

Unfortunately, I didn't realize that while my code failed, the `onMessage` functions were still registered, and despite the fact that my websocket object was removed, I hadn't registered `$finalize()`, so the `cnxOnMessage()` cancellation functions were not triggered. Again, my mistake. It took me a few minutes to realize why every line of streaming data was being written to file 16 times :-(

In other areas, I take a peek at `later:::list_queue()` to do manual cleanup when I mis-manage a cnx-function, but I could not find the websocket loop for its handling. While I've since added the `$finalize()` function to deregister `$onMessage()`, I wonder if there is any canonical way to view the private loop, potentially finding their IDs to cleanup the mess I created?

title: ability to run synchronously?
description:
I understand the intent and benefit of using `later` to run this in a separate thread. Understanding the thread component, I have a use-case where I'd like to reduce the latency as much as possible (and still do this in R). Is the best/only way to do this to repeatedly call `later::run_now()`? Is there a minimum interval imposed internally where running `run_now()` inside of this interval is unlikely to see incoming data?

Ideally it would be nice to have the ability to impose a blocking poll for incoming data.

title: Using several websockets with high incoming data rate and queues
description:
Hi,

I'm looking for an efficient pattern to do the following:
- I need to connect to several websocket which send a lot of data at a high rate (it's common to see 20-30 messages/second)
- I want to store the incoming data in queues, one for each websocket.
- then I have a main process which reads the queues and process them asynchronously.

Now here is my problem: in an ideal world, I would like to have one thread for each websocket and its queue and the main thread will read from the queue at its own rate. Now, I don't want to have slow IPC like in most of the R packages (futures, ipc, promises, etc...) which rely on local files. I need very fast communications (like shared memory for example).

How would you approach this problem?

(I know it's not an "issue" with websocket per se but it's still related to it, because I'd like to have not only the internal websocket in a thread but also the $onMessage method too)

**When running from unix shell script:**
**Using below R commands [ Rscript /path/to/myRprogram .R (OR) R -f /path/to/myRprogram .R]**
After ws <- WebSocket$new line execution, R does NOT listen for ws$onOpen ws$onMessage events.
It just runs rest of the code outside the functions ws$onOpen ws$onMessage etc, till the end and completely stops the program execution.

finalize = function() {

description:
Hi,

`WebSocket` is a great package. It does exactly what it supposes to do. And I found it more user-friendly than similar modules in phyton.

Its documentation, however, is not as complete as other rstudio's packages documentation. There's no way to guess how to call a great part of WebSockets arguments, like `protocols` or `headers`. Nevertheless, step by step I made the way to solve all the issues. Except from one: I could not find a way to return to main  thread after an error. As vignette states,

> The I/O for a WebSocket happens on a separate thread from the main R thread; there is one thread for each WebSocket.

When I get the most common error (the  `asio.ssl.stream:1(stream truncated)` error, code 1006), all the session gets paused, the websocket thread as well as the main thread. Basically, the entire script (or the entire set of instructions on an interactive sessión) stops to do anything. I just can't find a way to return to main thread from `onError` handler.

¿Any idea on how to solve this issue?

title: Websocket doesn't connect in batch mode
description:
When placing the following example into `tmp.R` and running with `R --vanilla --file=tmp.R` the websocket is not connecting:

```R
library(websocket)
ws <- WebSocket$new("ws://echo.websocket.org/",
                    autoConnect = FALSE)
ws$onMessage(function(event) {
  cat("Client got msg:", event$data, "\n")
})
ws$onClose(function(event) {
  cat("Client disconnected\n")
})
ws$onOpen(function(event) {
  cat("Client connected\n")
})
ws$connect()
while(T) {
  cat(".")
  Sys.sleep(1)
}
```
When that code is run directly at interactive session, same issue but the following error is thrown on interrupt after enough time has passed:

```
[2019-04-19 15:24:14] [info] Error getting remote endpoint: asio.system:9 (Bad file descriptor)
[2019-04-19 15:24:14] [info] asio async_shutdown error: asio.system:9 (Bad file descriptor)
[2019-04-19 15:24:14] [error] handle_connect error: Timer Expired
```

My real use case is a bit more involved. I am starting R process from java with `ProcessBuilder`. I can happily interact with the process but cannot start the websocket. In this case `ws$connect()` doesn't produce any output, not even an error.

title: Installation on Windows fails with MAKEFLAGS=-j4
WebSocket run with later private loop can sometimes not be GC'd
description:
Note: this needs the joe/feature/private-event-loops2 branch branch of later.

In this example, the websocket is created and closed, and driven from a private event loop. It calls `run_now()` until the websocket's has `readyState()==3`. If the `ws` object is removed and then a GC happens, the object is _not_ garbage collected. The event loop needs to be run one more time before the GC occurs.

```r
devtools::install_github("r-lib/later@joe/feature/private-event-loops2")

library(later)
library(WebSocket)

private_loop <- NULL
later::with_private_loop({
  private_loop <<- current_loop()
  ws <- WebSocket$new("ws://echo.websocket.org")
  reg.finalizer(ws, function(e) message("finalized!"))
  ws$close()
  while (ws$readyState() != 3L) {
    run_now()
  }
})

rm(ws)
gc()
#>           used (Mb) gc trigger (Mb) limit (Mb) max used (Mb)
#> Ncells  967903 51.7    1538886 82.2         NA  1538886 82.2
#> Vcells 2165223 16.6    8388608 64.0      16384  4722708 36.1

run_now(loop = private_loop)
gc()
#> finalized!
#>           used (Mb) gc trigger (Mb) limit (Mb) max used (Mb)
#> Ncells  967903 51.7    1538886 82.2         NA  1538886 82.2
#> Vcells 2165394 16.6    8388608 64.0      16384  4722708 36.1
```

This happens because `scheduleIncoming()` is always called right after `wsPoll()`, even if that `wsPoll()` call changes the readyState to 3 -- but then in the code above, the private loop doesn't get run again.

https://github.com/rstudio/websocket/blob/ccc03d59868b3ced956d54bd22dc4e89376dd207/R/websocket.R#L240-L247

title: Connection state is not Open until there pause in R session
description:
This is an odd issue I've run across in a couple of different platforms (details below). As best as I can tell, it was introduced by #16.

When I run the following command: 
`ws <- WebSocket$new("ws://echo.websocket.org/"); ws$readyState()`,
the response is `0L: Connecting`.

However, when running the the two commands separately, the response is `1L: Open`.

It is even such that inside Rstudio, when running `ws <- WebSocket$new("ws://echo.websocket.org/")` and then `ws$readyState()`, the response will be different depending on whether the two lines are both selected and run, or if they are run one at a time.

This issue manifests itself when sourcing a script. If the script were to contain:
```
ws <- WebSocket$new("ws://echo.websocket.org/")
ws$send("hello")
```
this would fail with the error message `Error in wsSend(private$wsObj, msg) : invalid state`. However, when run interactively, by running one line at a time, it would run without errors.

Finally, I'll note that I don't believe this is to be a timing issue per se. Instructing R to wait prior to checking the state (i.e. `ws <- WebSocket$new("ws://echo.websocket.org/"); Sys.sleep(5); ws$readyState()`) will still return `0L: Connecting`. title: WebsocketClient objects are not GC'd when there are no external references to them
description:
For example, this creates a WebsocketClient but doesn't bind it to a name, then GC's it.

```R
library(websocket)

WebsocketClient$new("ws://echo.websocket.org/")

gc()
```

Even after the `gc()`, it will periodically print logging information like this:

```
[2018-07-13 20:37:17] [control] Control frame received with opcode 9
[2018-07-13 20:37:17] [frame_header] Dispatching write containing 1 message(s) containing 6 header bytes and 0 payload bytes
[2018-07-13 20:37:17] [frame_header] Header Bytes: 
[0] (6) 8A 80 2C 35 82 20 
```

If a finalizer is added on the WebsocketClient instance, it doesn't run. This tells us that not only is the underlying C++ object still around; the R6 object is as well.

In this case, the connection stays open, and as long as it's open, `private$handleIncoming` will keep scheduling itself.

*****

Here's an example of a WebsocketClient objects that is closed, but not garbage collected. The "Finalized!" message is never printed. (The logging information doesn't get printed, though.)

```R
ws <- WebsocketClient$new("ws://echo.websocket.org/")
reg.finalizer(ws, function(e) cat("Finalized!\n"))
ws$close()
rm(ws)
gc()
```

title: Should allow empty onMessage method
description:
Sometimes it's useful to just send messages to a websocket. However, if `onMessage` isn't passed to the constructor, you get this error:

```
> WebsocketClient$new("ws://echo.websocket.org/")
Error in wsCreate(url, onMessage, onOpen, onClose, onFail) : 
  Cannot convert object to a function: [type=NULL; target=CLOSXP, SPECIALSXP, or BUILTINSXP].
```

The default `onMessage` method should essentially do nothing.

title: Rename onClose to onClosed?
description:
This is actually about to the websocketClient package: perhaps `onClose` should be renamed to `onClosed`, since it is called *after* the connection is disconnected, from either side?

I feel like `onClose` would be an appropriate name for a callback that's executed when the user calls `$close()`, before the connection is actually closed. I don't hold this opinion strongly, though.

title: Need to fix Windows compile issues
Should add ability to send closing code and reason
Tests timing should be fixed
description:
The tests in test-client.R work if you step through them, but not if they're run all at once.

It does things like this, where `last` is set by the `onMessage` handler. 

```R
  ws$send(charToRaw("hello"))
  expect_identical(last, charToRaw("hello"))
```

The problem is that the `expect_identical` is called before the response is received. It would be nice to be able to add a line like `waitfor(1)`, which returns if there's a response within one second (or if it has already occurred) and times out after one second.
